title: Compiled equality test
statement: Let $Z$ be compiler size data for word size $W$, with local-frame capacity $Z.F$, limits $Z.lim$, stack capacity $Z.Q$, and a memory layout and code layout as specified by $Z$. Let $[0m\sigma$ be a light state and let $q$ be a stack position such that memory $m$ represents $[0m\sigma$ in a frame at $q$, with $1 \le q$ and $q+Z.F \le Z.Q$. Suppose every location and memory value of $[0m\sigma$ has absolute value at most $Z.lim.word$, the code beginning at position $pos$ contains the compiled equality test for expressions $a,b$ with target position $l$, this condition has width at most $Z.F$, and both expressions are safe under $Z.lim$ in $[0m\sigma$. Then there is a final memory $m'$ and a number of steps $n$ no greater than the size of the equality condition such that execution from $pos$ reaches $pos$ plus that size if $a$ and $b$ have equal values in $[0m\sigma$, and reaches $l$ otherwise; throughout this execution, memory agrees with $m$ outside the scratch cells for a frame of size $Z.F$.
hypotheses_covered: Memory and state form a representation related by Rel at stack position q
The stack position satisfies 1 ≤ q and q + Z.F ≤ Z.Q

The equality condition width is at most Z.F
The equality condition is safe in σ under Z.lim
